bounded_purpose: Create, before any application implementation, a comprehensive product-UI design contract and visually reviewable protocol-workbench board for a GitHub-hosted, local-only interactive OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect learning site. Define foundations, components, protocol visual grammar, eight hands-on modules, milestone progression, all interaction states, responsive/touch/keyboard/reduced-motion behavior, accessibility, no-essay copy rules, synthetic fixtures, security feedback, and testable acceptance criteria. Do not create application source, packages, tests, workflows, screenshots, deployments, pushes, or publications; never present token decoding as signature verification.

failures_and_substitutions.detail: The earlier interactive brief expired before confirmation. It created no project, run, or repository files. The user explicitly authorized exactly one fresh skipped brief workflow.

With skip:true, Open Design's empty question form confirmed generic built-in defaults of Product UI, Evolve an existing brand, and Foundations + core components. This conflicted with the authoritative contract. The single Local Codex run prompt therefore explicitly enforced Product UI, Start fresh, and Comprehensive; no second brief workflow was created.
No callable in-app browser was available, so the live Studio URL could not be opened automatically. The Open Design run completed successfully and returned both Studio and preview URLs.

The user npm cache contains root-owned entries and returned EPERM before linting. The command was rerun with an isolated temporary npm cache; global ownership and repository configuration were not changed.

The Open Design source parsed with no errors but reported unsupported component sub-token warnings, orphan references, and contrast warnings. The repository DESIGN.md was corrected to alpha-spec-supported component keys and contrast-safe accent/warning roles. Final lint reported zero errors and zero warnings.
